title: Money Returned by the Operator, Excluded From the Prepaid Cost
content:
Money the operator has already given back to the traveller does not stand as prepaid cost when a
declaration on the Travel Protection Plans is corrected. What has been returned is read from the operator's
ledger for the packaged holiday held under the Vacation Package Products, together with the standing of that
holiday's record.

## The three readings

| What the ledger and the record show | What has been returned |
|---|---|
| The ledger carries money paid back to the traveller, and the record stands confirmed | The money paid back |
| The ledger carries a future travel credit issued in place of money, and no money paid back | The credit issued |
| Neither of those | Nothing |

## Points of judgement

Money paid back on a holiday whose record stands cancelled rather than confirmed reaches neither of the first
two readings, the second being closed because money was paid back, and nothing is taken out for what has been
returned. A holiday whose ledger carries both money paid back and a credit issued falls under the first reading
where its record stands confirmed, and the credit issued is not taken out alongside the money. A holiday whose
ledger carries a credit issued and no money paid back falls under the second whatever the standing of its
record.
